title: Unpatterned Wafer Inspection - CD Variation Detection on Zeta-20
subtitle: Final Inspection Quality Validation for 3nm Node Manufacturing
author: Michael Torres

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Zeta-20 system to detect and classify CD Variation defects during final inspection inspection at the 3nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab A to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for CD Variation defects that are critical to yield at the 3nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Zeta-20 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Zeta-20
- Inspection Type: Unpatterned Wafer Inspection
- Target Defect: CD Variation
- Process Step: Final Inspection
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 3nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab A

This test case applies to all Zeta-20 systems deployed at Milpitas Fab A for final inspection monitoring in the 3nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Zeta-20
Software Version: v10.5.419
Recipe: UNPATTERNED_WAFER_INSPECTION_3nm_FINAL INSPECTION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Medium (84 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Zeta-20 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Unpatterned Wafer Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target CD Variation defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 3nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 92 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 95% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.5% for Unpatterned Wafer Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.95 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-01-29
Wafers Tested: 8
Total Defects Found: 1849
Defect Density: 588.56 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 7.6%
Capture Rate: 89.9%
Test Duration: 206 minutes
System Uptime: 99.9%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Zeta-20 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting CD Variation at the 3nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Edge-zone defect detection showed improved performance compared to previous revision.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for CD Variation at 3nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
